finding: Table 14-3.01: the selection criteria and the SAS code select PARAMCD="ATOT", but the parameter list declares ACTOT, and no record in ADQSADAS has PARAMCD=ATOT.
evidence: Target pilot_arm_findings; ADQSADAS value-level metadata and data list ACTOT only.
cause: Typing error in the hand-written analysis results metadata. Run as written, the code would select no records.
decision: Use PARAMCD=ACTOT for the primary analysis. Our metadata will not repeat the error.

source: ADSL vs official ADSL (first comparison, unrounded)
variable: AVGDD; BMIBL; HEIGHTBL; WEIGHTBL; DURDIS; DURDSGR1
finding: Unrounded, our values differed for AVGDD (67 subjects), BMIBL (253), HEIGHTBL (204), WEIGHTBL (231) and DURDIS (254), e.g. HEIGHTBL 147.32 vs 147.3. Rounded with R's round(), 18 still differed (e.g. WEIGHTBL 56.25 -> 56.2 vs 56.3). BMIBL from unrounded height and weight differed for 28 subjects, and DURDSGR1 for one (01-710-1183: DURDIS 11.99, official >=12).
evidence: Target adsl_vs_official; tests round_sas in test-adam-helpers.R.
cause: The official ADSL stores floats with the define.xml's SignificantDigits (1 decimal) rounded half away from zero, as SAS ROUND does, and derives BMIBL, BMIBLGR1 and DURDSGR1 from the stored, rounded values. The define.xml says neither.
decision: round_sas() and round_to_spec(): every float with SignificantDigits is rounded as SAS does, and derivations that name an ADSL variable use its stored value.

source: Official ADSL vs define.xml codelist BMICAT
finding: The derivation text gives the groups as Normal, Overweight and Obese (the decodes of BMICAT). The official data hold codes instead: <25, 25-<30 and >=30. BMICAT's code for the third group is >30, which no record has, and which contradicts the rule BMIBL >= 30.
evidence: Target pilot_spec_findings (value not in codelist); test-define.R and test-adsl.R.
cause: Inconsistent hand-written metadata: the codelist's code >30 is a typing error for >=30, and the derivation text names the decodes.
decision: Store the codes, as Define-XML expects, with >=30 for the third group, following the derivation rule. Our check reports the value as not in the codelist, which is expected. Our own metadata will code it >=30.

finding: Subject 01-702-1082 has no baseline weight, so BMIBL is missing. The official ADSL gives BMIBLGR1 = <25; ours is missing.
cause: In SAS a missing number is smaller than any number, so a condition BMIBL < 25 is true for it. The derivation text excludes it (. < BMIBL < 25), but the official program did not.
decision: Keep BMIBLGR1 missing, as the derivation says. A subject with no BMI must not be counted as normal weight.

finding: The derivation names SC.SCTESTCD = YEARSEDU, but the pilot's SC has a single test code, EDLEVEL (years of education, one record per subject).
evidence: SDTM sc.xpt: table(SCTESTCD) gives EDLEVEL only.
cause: The define.xml was written against a different version of the SC test codes.
decision: Use SCTESTCD = EDLEVEL. The result matches the official ADSL for all 254 subjects.

finding: The derivation reads WEIGHTBL / ((HEIGHTBL*100)**2), which with height in cm gives values near 3e-7, not BMI. The official BMIBL values are BMI in kg/m2.
evidence: Target adsl_vs_official: with WEIGHTBL / (HEIGHTBL/100)**2 our BMIBL matches the official for all 253 subjects with a value.
cause: Typing error in the derivation text: *100 for /100.
decision: Use WEIGHTBL / (HEIGHTBL/100)**2, the BMI formula for height in cm.

finding: The derivation subsets to CQ01NAM='' and TRTEMFL='Y', but describes the flag as the first treatment-emergent dermatologic event. Read literally, it would flag the first non-dermatologic event. The official ADAE flags dermatologic events only (152 records, all with CQ01NAM = DERMATOLOGIC EVENTS).
evidence: Official adae.xpt: table(AOCC01FL, CQ01NAM); target adae_vs_official shows no difference for AOCC01FL.
cause: Typing error in the derivation text: CQ01NAM='' for CQ01NAM ne ''.
decision: Follow the description: subset to CQ01NAM = DERMATOLOGIC EVENTS. Our AOCC01FL matches the official for all 1191 records.

finding: Four events of subject 01-716-1418 (AESEQ 5 to 8) start in July 2013 with no day (ASTDT imputed to 2013-07-01, ASTDTF = D) and have an end date. Ours gives ADURN 88 or 96 days and ADURU = DAY; the official leaves both missing.
evidence: Target adae_vs_official; test-adae.R. These are the only records with an imputed start date and an end date.
cause: The official program does not compute a duration from an imputed start date. The define.xml gives ADURN = AENDT - ASTDT + 1 with no such exception.
decision: Follow the specification and compute ADURN. ASTDTF shows the start date is imputed, so a reader can exclude these durations. Our own specification will state the rule either way.

finding: In 19 subjects a second ADAS-Cog assessment falls in the same window as an earlier one and is not analysed (ANL01FL blank). The official ADQSADAS replaces its observed total with the previous value and marks it DTYPE = LOCF (e.g. 01-701-1294, day 83: QS total 6, official 14). The next windows without an assessment then carry that record's date and visit, so 33 LOCF records have a different ADT, ADY and VISITNUM from ours.
evidence: Targets adqsadas_vs_official (19 values, 33 records only in one side); test-adqsadas.R. The analysed records (ANL01FL = Y, 1016) have the same AVAL in both datasets.
cause: The official program applies LOCF to every record after the first in a window, not only to empty windows, and carries forward from the last record rather than the analysed one. The SAP (8.2) says imputation uses the targeted assessment within each window.
decision: Keep observed values as observed; create LOCF records only for windows with no assessment, carrying the analysed assessment of the last window before it, with its date. The values used in the analyses are unchanged.

finding: The value-level metadata of ACTOT say: set QSSEQ to missing for post-baseline records. The official ADQSADAS keeps QS's QSSEQ for all 786 post-baseline ACTOT records, LOCF records included.
evidence: Target adqsadas_vs_official (QSSEQ, 753 records with the same key); value-level metadata ADQSADAS.QSSEQ.ACTOT.
cause: The official program did not apply this rule.
decision: Follow the specification: QSSEQ is missing for post-baseline totals, which are derived from the items, not taken from QS.

finding: Baseline BMI groups: the report has <25 = 47 (56%) in the low dose and 150 (59%) in total, 25-<30 = 27 (32%) in the low dose, and p = 0.2326. Ours: 46 (55%), 149 (59%), 27 (33%) and p = 0.2235. The other 56 of the 58 rows match cell by cell.
evidence: Target t_14_2_01_vs_csr; test-tables.R. Counting the subject with no BMI as <25 reproduces the report exactly.
cause: D-004 carried into the table: subject 01-702-1082 has no BMI and is counted as <25, with 84 instead of 83 as the denominator.
decision: Keep the subject out of the BMI groups, as in our ADSL (D-004).

finding: Four Fisher's exact p-values differ in the third decimal: vomiting, high dose 0.208 vs 0.209; salivary hypersecretion 0.057 vs 0.058; application site erythema 0.002 vs 0.003; syncope, low dose 0.057 vs 0.058. All counts, percentages and event counts of the 254 rows match.
evidence: Target t_14_5_01_vs_csr; test-tables.R, which checks that rounding twice reproduces the four printed values.
cause: The report rounded the p-values twice, to 4 and then to 3 decimals (0.208498 -> 0.2085 -> 0.209). The exact p-values agree.
decision: Round once. The four printed values are off by one in the last digit.

source: define.xml analysis results metadata vs study report p. 49
finding: The SAS code in the analysis results metadata fits the dose response as CHG = TRTPN SITEGR1, with no baseline value. The table's footnote [1] says the ANCOVA has baseline as a covariate. Without baseline the p-value is 0.253; with it, 0.245, the printed value.
evidence: Target t_14_3_01_vs_csr; test-tables.R fits both models.
cause: The hand-written metadata leave the covariate out of the code; the report was produced with it.
decision: Fit the model of the footnote, CHG = dose + site group + baseline. Our metadata will hold the code that produced the output.

source: Pinnacle 21 Community ADaM-IG 1.0 (FDA 2204.1), our and official XPT, pilot define.xml
variable: SEX; DISCONFL; DSRAEFL; DTHFL; AOCCFL; AOCCSFL; AOCCPFL; AOCC01FL; AOCC02FL; AOCC03FL; AOCC04FL; ABLFL; ANL01FL
finding: Rule SD0037: every SEX value (M, F) and every Y of the flags is reported as not in its codelist (SEX, Y_BLANK), in all four datasets: e.g. SEX 254 in ADSL, ANL01FL 12103 in ADQSADAS.
evidence: P21 reports ours-full.xlsx and official-full.xlsx (studies/benchmark/output/p21/, not in git); identical counts in both; see studies/benchmark/conformance.md
cause: The define.xml codes are padded with a non-breaking space (U+00A0): SEX has 'F<U+00A0>', 'M<U+00A0>', 'U<U+00A0>' and Y_BLANK has 'Y<U+00A0>'. Pinnacle 21 compares exactly, so no value matches. Our reader already trims this padding (R/define_v1.R).
decision: Data unchanged: M, F and Y are the correct values. Our own define.xml (phase F3) must not pad codes.

source: Pinnacle 21 Community ADaM-IG 1.0 (FDA 2204.1), our and official XPT, pilot define.xml

cause: Same cause as D-003: the codelist has '>30', while the data and the SAP group are '>=30'.

source: Pinnacle 21 Community ADaM-IG 1.0 (FDA 2204.1), our and official XPT, pilot define.xml

source: Pinnacle 21 Community ADaM-IG 1.0 (FDA 2204.1), our and official XPT, pilot define.xml
